questions.answer: The reliability of the belief-forming process, subject to the specific theory.
questions.feedback: Check the definition and explain it in your own words before retrying.

questions.prompt: What does a safety condition investigate?
questions.answer: Whether a true belief could easily have been false in relevant nearby circumstances.
questions.feedback: Check the distinction or calculation against the worked case; correct the first unsupported step.

questions.prompt: Why compare theories on the same case?
questions.answer: It isolates how their different proposed conditions affect judgement.
questions.feedback: State a concrete implication or limitation and retry without notes.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Applies multiple accounts to a shared case and explains disagreements without oversimplifying.
scoring.transfer: Construct a new fictional case and compare three theories using the same facts. Identify a counterexample or objection and explicitly preserve disagreements.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
